sentences.text: Caseosaurus was a small, lightly built, bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore that could reach a length of 2 meters; however, its classification remains debated, with some studies placing it outside the Dinosauria.

Size estimates indicate Caseosaurus grew up to 2 meters long and weighed no more than 50 kilograms, though its placement within or outside the Dinosauria is a subject of ongoing scientific discussion.
The genus Caseosaurus was formally described and named by Hunt, Lucas, Heckert, Sullivan, and Lockley in 1998.
The genus name Caseosaurus means "Case's lizard" and honors the scientist Ermine Cowles Case.
The specific name crosbyensis refers to Crosby County in Texas, where the fossils were discovered.
In 2018, Caseosaurus was re-evaluated as a valid species identified as a relative of Herrerasaurus, placing it outside the Dinosauria.
In 2004, Langer examined the holotype ilium and reassigned it to the genus Chindesaurus.
The paleoenvironment of Caseosaurus included the archosaur Tecovasaurus and other early theropods that left preserved bipedal tracks.
Irmis et al. concluded that an ilium originally assigned to Eucoelophysis strongly resembles the Caseosaurus holotype.
A recent review classified Caseosaurus as a nomen dubium, contradicting earlier studies that validated it.
